summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted after being brought back by EMS due to inability to transfer to her wheelchair at home, following a recent discharge against medical advice during treatment for E. coli bacteremia. She was restarted on IV Zosyn to complete a 14-day antibiotic course. A CT scan revealed a 1.2 cm left renal stone with perirenal inflammation, but urology recommended outpatient follow-up without immediate intervention. Her acute kidney injury and transaminitis improved during the stay, with labs trending toward baseline. She developed transient antibiotic-associated diarrhea, which resolved spontaneously and tested negative for C. difficile. Physical therapy recommended home services after she declined inpatient rehabilitation. She was discharged on oral Bactrim, with plans for outpatient follow-up for urology, liver evaluation, and lymph node monitoring, along with home physical therapy.
